posts.title: Inflation Shrinks What Your Cash Buys – Invest Money You Won’t Need for 5 Years
posts.description: Inflation, the steady rise in prices, shrinks what each dollar you hold in cash can buy, even at the modest pace the Federal Reserve aims for. Keep your emergency fund and money you’ll spend within five years in savings, and invest the rest, since stocks have grown faster than prices over long periods. Source

posts.title: A Cheaper City Weekend – Stay Near a Train Line and Do the Pass Math
posts.description: On a city weekend, book a room near a train line rather than downtown, ride transit instead of paying to park, and plan your days around sights that are free for visitors. Buy an attractions pass only if the places you’ll see would cost more at the gate. Source

posts.title: 15 Active Jobs for People Who Hate Sitting – Weigh Pay Against Physical Toll
posts.description: Plenty of jobs pay you to walk, lift, and climb instead of sitting, and some pay well above the typical U.S. wage. Before you switch, compare each job’s pay and training with what it asks of your body, since the active jobs you can start fastest tend to pay the least. Source
